headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Chatwoot’s customer data can flow into gpt-engineer’s writable project workspace and be acted on without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, while gpt-engineer reads and writes a project directory with no default self-isolation. If Chatwoot content is copied into files or prompts, malicious instructions can reach gpt-engineer through that shared workspace. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or files
IF the project directory contains attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Use a separate scratch directory for pasted content
Strip instructions from customer messages before handoff
Review generated files before any execution
Disable copy-paste of raw support transcripts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and gpt-engineer has broad network egress plus filesystem access in the project directory. That creates a plausible path for sensitive support data to be written into generated code or sent to a third-party model backend. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach.
conditions: IF customer transcripts or orders are placed into the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer forwards those contents to its model backend
mitigations: Keep customer data out of the coding workspace
Redact PII before any prompt or file handoff
Use a local-only model for the coding agent
Restrict outbound network access during runs
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss prevention on the project directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support system with API integrations, while gpt-engineer can execute shell commands, install packages, and write files in a per-project directory. Their overlap on mutable project state can cause conflicting writes or accidental overwrites if both touch the same workspace. The shared-directory concurrency model makes this plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF Chatwoot exports or syncs artifacts into that directory
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Freeze the workspace before gpt-engineer runs
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Use version control checkpoints before changes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing messages, reports, and interaction history, and gpt-engineer is designed to write files and offer to run generated code. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input, gpt-engineer can turn unverified support content into code or operational artifacts, creating downstream mistakes with real impact. No verification step is shown in either profile.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is used as a source of truth for code generation
IF generated artifacts are executed or deployed
mitigations: Require human review of all generated artifacts
Separate factual extraction from code generation
Mark Chatwoot outputs as untrusted input
Run generated code only in a disposable sandbox
requires-engineering: add validation gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and messages, while gpt-engineer handles files in a user-specified project directory and can send content to a configured model backend. If EU or regulated customer data is placed into that workspace, residency and retention obligations can be violated because the coding agent’s backend location and logging policy are not specified. Uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied into the coding workspace
IF the configured model backend stores prompts or logs outside required jurisdictions
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace
Use a residency-approved backend only
Minimize logs and prompt retention
Document retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls
